title: Kissed with Pineapple Thai Chicken Khao-Soi
description: A funky, crunchy, and energizing Thai dish featuring spherified pineapple juice and a low-fat friendly twist on the classic Khao-Soi recipe from Northern Thailand. This dish is a perfect combination of flavors and textures, making it a great option for a quick and delicious meal.
instructions: Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat, then add the chicken breast and cook until browned on all sides and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes, or until the internal temperature reaches 165°F (74°C).
Remove the chicken from the skillet and set aside to rest.
Add the coconut milk, fish sauce, sambal oelek, kaffir lime leaves, galangal, and Thai red curry paste to the skillet and stir to combine.
Bring the mixture to a simmer and cook for 2-3 minutes, or until the sauce has thickened slightly.
Add the roasted peanuts and stir to combine.
Add the rice noodles to the skillet and stir to combine.
Cook for 2-3 minutes, or until the noodles are heated through.
Slice the chicken into thin strips and return it to the skillet.
Stir to combine with the sauce and noodles.
Season with salt to taste.

Transfer the Khao-Soi to a serving wooden-board and garnish with chopped fresh cilantro, fried shallots, spherified pineapple juice, pickled carrots and daikon, crushed peanuts, and a lime wedge on the side.
Serve immediately and enjoy!
To make the spherified pineapple juice, place the pineapple juice in a saucepan and heat it over medium heat until it reaches 180°F (82°C).
Remove the saucepan from the heat and let it cool slightly.
Add 1/4 cup of sodium alginate to the pineapple juice and stir to combine.
Using a syringe or piping bag, drop the pineapple juice mixture into a bath of cold water.
Stir the water gently to create a whirlpool effect, then drop the mixture into the center of the whirlpool.
The mixture will form into small, round spheres.
Let the spheres sit in the cold water for 5-10 minutes, or until they have firmed up and are no longer sticky.
Remove the spheres from the water and pat them dry with paper towels.
Slice the spheres in half just before serving.
Note: this recipe is for refrigerator pickling/preserving only — store in the refrigerator and consume within 1 week. Do not water-bath can without an acid (vinegar or lemon juice).
